fact: Procurement Policy Office Directive No 47 says the 55 listed public bodies must undertake all their procurement through the e-Procurement System.

The directive gives effect to mandatory use of the e-Procurement System by all public bodies, with other bodies to be fully on board by 31 December 2020, and paper only for exceptions such as minor works.

The AfDB/MAPS assessment says Mauritius' e-Procurement System (e-PS) went live on 28 September 2015 with the first electronic Invitation for Bid, published by the Mauritius Police Force, and bidding runs through it.
The assessment says Mauritian law mandates the e-PS for all open advertised bidding and requires all public bodies to use it, while finding use selective and bid evaluation and award often offline.

The Procurement Policy Office says the web-based e-Procurement System (e-PS), launched in September 2015, covers the procurement process, with use made mandatory by government from July 2020, and 116 of 205 public bodies used it in 2023/24.

The Procurement Policy Office says the e-PS expert recommended procuring a new enhanced e-PS, and preparatory action on replacing it with an electronic Government Procurement System (e-GP) is the next phase, with AfDB-approved terms of reference.

The Procurement Policy Office reports that in 2023/24 public bodies published 7,681 electronic invitations for bids, received 18,599 electronic bid submissions, and awarded 4,938 contracts above Rs 100,000 through the e-PS against 3,819 paper-based.
The Ministry of ICT says the sovereign cloud RFI document may be downloaded from the Public Procurement Portal (publicprocurement.govmu.org), which publishes government procurement documents online.
